name: Tree Pose
hero_alt: Tree Pose, seen from the front
meta_description: Standing knee bending, hips uneven, torso leaning, head tilting to balance? Three things usually hold back Tree Pose, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
og_description: Three things usually hold back Tree Pose, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
lede: Standing leg strong, hips level, torso tall and centered, head steady. Here’s the rubric Posewise measures it against, and what to train when you miss.
rubric_intro: Posewise checks four things from the front. Here’s what good looks like.

rubric.name: Standing leg
rubric.good: Straight and strong, knee not locked

rubric.name: Hips
rubric.good: Level, neither side hiking or dropping

rubric.name: Torso
rubric.good: Tall and centered over the standing foot

rubric.name: Head
rubric.good: Level, gaze on one still point

fixes.why: The standing-leg glutes hold the pelvis level on one leg. When they’re weak, the hips tip and the torso leans to compensate.
fixes.cue: Level your hips and stand tall over your foot.

fixes.outcome: your standing leg will stay straight and strong.
fixes.why: A standing knee that softens as you hold usually points to single-leg strength running out.
fixes.cue: Press down through your standing foot.

faq.q: Can I put my foot on my knee in Tree Pose?
faq.a: No. Place it above or below the knee, on your inner thigh or calf, so there’s no sideways pressure on the joint.

faq.q: Why do I lose my balance in Tree Pose?
faq.a: Usually a wandering gaze or a weak standing hip. Fix your eyes on one still point and press your foot and inner leg into each other.

faq.q: Why does my foot slide down in Tree Pose?
faq.a: Press your foot and leg into each other with equal force, or start with your foot on your calf or your toes on the floor.

faq.q: Should my hips be level in Tree Pose?
faq.a: Yes. The lifted-leg hip tends to hike up, so draw it down until both hip points face forward and sit level.

faq.q: How can I check my Tree Pose form at home?
faq.a: Film yourself from the front. Or use Posewise, an iPhone app that measures your Tree Pose with the camera, speaks corrections as you hold it, and builds a six-minute daily plan for what it finds.

llms_summary: the three things that usually hold back Tree Pose (outer-hip strength for level hips and an upright torso, quad strength for a straight standing leg, core strength for a steady head and balance), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
cues: And one cue: fix your gaze on one still point ahead and keep your head level. A steady gaze steadies everything below it.
